opus.why: A standard full-stack feature with tests. Streaming 200k+ rows needs care (cursor or streaming body, transaction scope), but it's well-trodden work that Sonnet handles fully at high effort.

fable.why: Well-specified multi-layer feature (endpoint, streaming service, frontend button, tests). Streaming without buffering needs care but is a standard pattern; sonnet at high covers it with no quality loss.

opus.why: The log already shows the N+1 clearly. The fix is batch fetching or an entity graph for items and products, plus batching the shipment lookups. The catch is that a fetch join on a collection combined with pagination silently pages in memory, so high effort is worth it, but this doesn't need Opus.

fable.why: Log makes the N+1 obvious; the real work is fixing it correctly in JPA (fetch joins/batch size vs pagination-in-memory pitfall, shipments lookup). Sonnet high handles that trap; medium risks a naive fetch-join that breaks paging.

opus.why: The design was already agreed in the earlier turn. Wiring it touches several pipeline steps (schema, planner, image and video prompt builders) and needs real use of the field, not a pass-through. It's moderate multi-file work that Sonnet handles well.

fable.why: Continues an agreed design but requires wiring a new field through planner, schema validation, and image/video prompt construction where the pacing must actually shape generation prompts. Visual-output prompt quality plus multi-component integration warrants opus.

opus.why: A security-heavy spec: SSRF protection with private-IP checks after DNS resolve (rebinding risk), secrets stored encrypted and shown once, constant-time HMAC verification, a customer-facing SDK helper, and async delivery via the job queue. Security mistakes here are costly.

fable.why: Security-sensitive spec: SSRF defence with post-DNS private-IP rejection, secret encryption at rest, HMAC with constant-time compare and replay window, async delivery via job queue, customer-facing SDK helper. Subtle mistakes here are costly, so opus.

opus.why: Breaking up a 1400-line class while keeping the public API unchanged and tests green without edits requires careful reading of hidden coupling and shared state. This is architectural refactoring where a subtle slip breaks three consuming modules.

fable.why: Splitting a 1400-line billing class into three without changing the public API or any test, with a stop-and-ask constraint. Large, precision-heavy refactor in billing/tax logic where regressions matter; needs opus-level care across the whole file.

opus.why: A cross-cutting storage migration: presigned URL security (expiry, content-type and size constraints, access control), a script migrating existing files, env config, and a frontend rewrite to direct upload. Architecture and security decisions matter here.

fable.why: Storage architecture migration: presigned upload/download design (scoping, size/content-type limits), data migration script, env config, and frontend rework to direct upload. Architecture plus security surface, so opus.

opus.why: Mostly a mechanical rename across layers. The backward-compatible migration (old column stays readable for one release) and the exclusion of the analytics module need care, but the work is well-specified and within Sonnet's range.

fable.why: Wide mechanical rename across API, DB migration with one-release backward compatibility, and TS types, with an exclusion zone. Mostly thoroughness rather than deep reasoning; sonnet high is sufficient to sweep completely and keep the migration safe.

opus.why: Extracting tokens and unifying the PDF and web renderers is architectural work, and the existing client's output must stay pixel-identical. Tracking down the padding drift between the two renderers without regressing the shipped PDF is subtle, and the result is client-facing.

fable.why: Brand-tooling refactor with three coupled parts: extract per-client tokens, unify PDF and web preview rendering that currently drift, add loud validation, all while keeping the shipped client output pixel-identical. Visual fidelity plus architecture; opus needed.

opus.why: The perf problems are obvious from the code: JSON.stringify and formatRelative recomputed on every keystroke, no memoization, index keys, and an inline style object plus callback on every card. useMemo, useDeferredValue, React.memo and stable keys fix it with no new library. Routine React work.

fable.why: Single-file React perf fix with clear culprits (JSON.stringify per render, index keys, per-render formatting, inline style objects, no memo/deferred value). Well-scoped and standard; sonnet medium delivers the same fix as a larger model.
